02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 03.07.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, while the petitioner was returning to his native place (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 (Dugganakunte to Beedaganahalli Village) in his TVS Motor Bike bearing No.KA-40-Y-9769 on the left side of the road, when he reached near Kodipalli Cross, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar, at about 09.30 p.m, the rider of Splendor Plus Motor Bike bearing No. KA-07-EE-8150 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Gownapalli Government hospital, after that he was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 9 days and has undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards transportation charges and medical expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, the petitioner not to do driving and labour work and he is the only bread earner of the family.
Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as tractor driver and labour and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Bike bearing No.KA-07-EE-8150 involved in the accident and in this regard the Gownapalli Police have registered a case against rider of the said offending (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 Motor Bike.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the said offending Motor Bike,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and have filed written statement.

04. Respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Splendor Plus Motor Bike bearing No.KA-07-EE-8150 and liability to indemnify the respondent Munireddy N vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190392605/
2 No.2 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and contended that the petitioner himself was solely responsible for the alleged accident and there is a delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint and petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident, as such he violated Sec.129 of M.V. Act and the rider of Splendor Plus Motor Bike was not holding valid and (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 effective driving licence to ride particular class of vehicle as on the date of accident and thereby, the owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, income,
occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

Further he admits that he is the R.C.
Owner of the Splendor Plus Motor Bike bearing No.KA-07-EE-8150 and the same was duly insured with respondent No.1 vide Policy No.3397/02288300/000/00 which is valid from 22.03.2021 to 20.03.2026 and the same was in force as on the date of accident.
If the court comes to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation, then the respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

The alleged accident occurred on the fault of the petitioner who was riding his Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and himself dashed against the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 respondent No.2's Motor Bike and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of his vehicle.

The compensation claimed is excessive, exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2.
06.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner prove that the he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 03.07.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, near Kodipalli Cross,
Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar, due to rash and negligent act of riding of the two-wheeler bearing registration No. KA-07-EE-8150 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?
07. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The respondent No.1 got examined MRO as RW.1 and through him got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.

sentences.text: The learned counsels for the petitioner and respondent No.1 have argued on main matter.

Despite sufficient opportunity has been given, the respondent No.2 did not advanced his arguments,
hence respondent No.2 side arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.1 counsel he denied to the suggestion that since he do not know riding of the Motor Cycle, he himself skid and fall and (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 sustained injuries and offending Motor Cycle was falsely implicated in the case and admits that as per Ex.P.9 Discharge summary there is no mention of the fact that he is undergone any surgery and also admits that in Ex.P.12 Medical bills,
the advance bills are also included in final bill and as per Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card he is aged about 39 years.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 15 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 15
on his behalf
. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR filed by the Gownapalli Police against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is copy of the Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report which discloses both vehicles are involved in the alleged accident and front side of both vehicles are damaged.

Ex.P.5 is copy of Charge sheet, which discloses that the Investigation Officer after through investigation has submitted the Charge sheet against the rider offending Motor Cycle for rash and negligent riding, causing accident and grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.6 is copy of bond executed by the accused.
Ex.P.7 is copy of bond executed by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of Wound Certificate, which shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.9 is Discharge summary of R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar,
which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient on 04.07.2023 and discharged on 11.07.2023 for 8 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.10 is CT brain report.
Ex.P.14 is CT scan and Ex.P.15 is X-ray.

12. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 03.07.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, near Kodipalli Cross, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar, due Munireddy N vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190392605/
4 to rash and negligent act of riding of Splendor Plus Motor Bike bearing No.KA-07-EE-8150, by its rider as alleged in the petition.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as tractor driver and labour and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards transportation (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 charges and medical expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to work and has become permanent disabled.
14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
But he has produced Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the said document can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 15.04.1984.
The alleged accident occurred on 03.07.2023.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 39 years.
15. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not produced any evidence or documents regarding his avocation and income.

Moreover, in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to establish that he has sustained any physical or functional disability due to accidental injuries and there is no evidence on record to show that he sustained loss of future income (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 or loss of income during laid up period and there is no evidence on record to show that he has required further treatment or surgery and as per Ex.P.9 as admitted by the PW.1 there is no mention of the fact that he is undergone any surgery and he has not sustained any amputation.

As per Ex.P.12 Medical bills totalling to Rs.37,644/-, but in the cross- examination,
PW.1 admits that as per Ex.P.12 Medical bills, the advance bills are also included in the final bill and on perusal of Ex.P.12 Medical bills, the advance bills are also included in the final bill.

Therefore,
after deducting the amount of Rs.19,000/- paid towards advance bills, the remaining Medical bills amount was Rs.18,644/-.
Therefore, in the absence of disability certificate, evidence of doctor, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/-.
16. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

17. Regarding liability:- On behalf of the respondent No.1 Insurance Company,s the MRO of R.L.
Jalappa hospital, Kolar, is examined as RW.1 and he has produced MLC extract and Police intimation as (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 per Ex.R.2 and 3 and during the course of cross- examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that as per Ex.R.3 Police intimation there is mention of RTA two-wheeler V/s two-wheeler and also admits that there is no mention of consumed alcohol by the rider of the Motor Cycle in the said documents and said documents and evidence of Munireddy N vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190392605/
5 RW.1 is no way helpful to the case of the respondents.

sentences.text: Further, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not lead their evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove their contentions.

Further, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company in its written statement at para 2 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending Motor Cycle and the same is valid as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 in his written statement at para 5 admits that he is the owner of the offending Motor Cycle and same was insured with respondent No.1 and policy is valid as on the date of accident.
But the respondent No.1 has not lead any evidence or placed any material to show that the owner or rider of the offending vehicle have violated terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore,
under the facts and circumstances of the case, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.5553/2023 pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending Motor Cycle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
